title: Savannah Guthrie Shares New Post Asking for Information About Her Mother’s Disappearance: ‘We Ache for Her, We Cry Out for Answers’
description: Savannah Guthrie has taken to social media to urge anyone with knowledge about her mother, Nancy, who was presumed kidnapped in February and has ye
body:
Savannah Guthrie has taken to social media to urge anyone with knowledge about her mother, Nancy, who was presumed kidnapped in February and has yet to be found, to come forward.

	Guthrie shared a drawing to her Instagram account done by her daughter that shows an umbrella, raindrops and the text: “I know it might not seem like it, but I really need my mommy.” Accompanying the photo was a caption, in which Gutherie wrote that the drawing “says so much about how I feel.”
	

	“The world goes on, things appear ‘normal’ – as we try to keep going and be strong, especially for our young kids – but it’s not and it never will be,” Guthrie’s caption continued. “For Annie and Tommy, for Cam and Kristine, for Mike and me and for all of mom’s beloved grandchildren: we ache for her, we cry out for answers, we cannot move forward. We need someone to help us, tell us what you know. Our mom was a light in this world. We want to celebrate her and give her the dignity she deserves. The reward is still available. Please. We are begging you. Please help us.”

	She concluded: “Thank you to all those who have been kind and shown the best of humanity. Join us in praying without ceasing.”

	In August, Guthrie shared a post to commemorate 6 months since her mother was kidnapped. “We have lived every moment, every breath, and every heartbeat in agony and despair ever since,” she wrote. “Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on — because that’s what our joyful and resilient Mom taught us to do.”

	One month before that, Guthrie had posted a video to Instagram directly addressing her mother’s kidnappers. “I’m coming on today with a very specific message. It has been months since our mom was taken from us. Our family is in agony. We are in a nightmare that will not end. Nothing about our situation has changed,” the “Today” host said. “We have done our part, and we will never stop looking for her. We will always ache for her and feel that hole in our hearts.”
	

	Nancy went missing on Feb. 1 after she missed her usual Sunday church service. The next day, the Pima County Sheriff’s Department called her disappearance a presumed kidnapping after they found concerning evidence at her home in Tucson, Ariz. The FBI joined in the search for Nancy and posted a $100,000 reward for information leading to her recovery. It was later increased to $200,000 and then $1 million on Feb. 24.

schema.headline: Savannah Guthrie Shares New Post Asking for Information About Her Mother’s Disappearance: ‘We Ache for Her, We Cry Out for Answers’

title: Harry Styles Closes Out 30-Night Madison Square Garden Residency With Two ‘Harryween’ Shows, Dressed as Elvis and Pizza Rat, and a Jalen Brunson Guest Appearance
description: Harry Styles record-setting 30-night residency at New York’s Madison Square Garden came to a close over the weekend, with a pair of Styles’ recurri
body:
Harry Styles record-setting 30-night residency at New York’s Madison Square Garden came to a close over the weekend, with a pair of Styles’ recurring “Harryween” concerts that saw the star, his band and much of the audience dressed for the occasion — in his case as 1970s-era Elvis Presley on the first night and the notorious “Pizza Rat” on the second, which also included an onstage appearance from basketball star Jalen Brunson, captain of the world champion New York Knicks, presenting Styles with a banner commemorating the residency.
	



	

	



	The themed costumes were not limited to the singer: On Friday, Styles’ band was dressed in his own iconic looks, rocking outfits based on his Coachella, Met Gala and Grammy appearances. “The theme on stage tonight was favorite sequined king,” he joked, later thanking the audience for considering him part of that group. For the encore, the arena was taken back in time as he emerged in his 2010 “X-Factor” audition outfit, singing Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely.” His version of the song was what clinched the then-bakery-worker a spot in One Direction over 15 years ago.


	The final show on Saturday was, in its entirety, a tribute to New York City. The band took the stage first, all dressed as local icons including the Statue of Liberty, Andy Warhol and Anna Wintour, before Styles himself appeared as “Pizza Rat,” based on a notorious 2015 meme showing a large rat dragging a slice of pizza down the stairs of a New York City subway station. In another nod to the city, this time in the form of music history, the pop star delivered a compelling cover of Talking Heads’ “Psycho Killer” before reverting to the standard setlist.
	

	The capstone of the evening came as New York Knicks captain Jalen Brunson took the stage to present Styles with a banner commemorating his record-breaking achievement. “I just wanted to appear and congratulate you on your 30th night,” said Brunson. “A couple weeks ago, Harry was so kind to join me and my team on our banner night, and I thought I, on behalf of MSG and the Knicks, would do the same.”


	Over the course of the nine-week residency, whether it was the occasional fan encounter on the Williamsburg Bridge or one of many fan-organized events (including One Direction karaoke and a post-Harryween bar crawl), the singer’s presence could be felt across the city, thanks in part to tour sponsor AmEx, which ran pop-up shops across lower Manhattan through the full nine-week block, and, halfway through the residency, invited ten randomly selected fans to experience “Together, Together” live for the first time.



	

	



	As the final show ended, Styles addressed the audience, saying: “You’ve been wonderful tonight — you’ve been wonderful every night. Thank you for showing up, for dressing up, for making us feel so loved and being so wonderful to us. Thank you so much. You’ve changed my life over and over again, and I get to remember every moment in here. I have loved it so much… Thank you for dancing with me. When I wrote this album, I wanted it to feel exactly like this.”

	The “Together, Together” tour will head to Australia later this month, where Styles will perform his final shows of the year, later resuming in the U.S. in April 2027 and slated to conclude in August with three consecutive shows at Wembley Stadium.

schema.headline: Harry Styles Closes Out 30-Night Madison Square Garden Residency With Two ‘Harryween’ Shows, Dressed as Elvis and Pizza Rat, and a Jalen Brunson Guest Appearance

title: ‘SNL’ Celebrates Milwaukee Brewers’ World Series Win With Bobby Moynihan’s Drunk Uncle on Weekend Update
description: “Saturday Night Live” paid tribute to the Milwaukee Brewers’ historic World Series win during a Weekend Update segment that featured the return of
body:
“Saturday Night Live” paid tribute to the Milwaukee Brewers’ historic World Series win during a Weekend Update segment that featured the return of Bobby Moynihan’s Drunk Uncle commentator character.

	Moynihan spent nine seasons on “SNL,” from 2009 to 2017. His recurring Drunk Uncle character was a classic Archie Bunker-esque East Coast guy with blunt observations on pop culture and politics. He last portrayed Drunk Uncle last year on “Saturday Night Live’s” 50th anniversary special.
	

	This time around, Drunk Uncle hailed the Brewers’ first World Series victory in the nearly 60-year history of the team as a win attributed to the power of suds in a town that is synonymous with beer — hence the team’s name.

	In classic fashion, Drunk Uncle told “Weekend Update” anchors Colin Jost and Michael Che that he was happy for the Brewers but deeply concerned about the state of baseball overall. After recent rule changes, the duration of most baseball games as tightened up, something that Drunk Uncle lamented. Instead of running seven hours, “the game ends in 20 minutes and everybody goes home to watch their gay hockey shows,” Moynihan as Drunk Uncle said in a nod to “Heated Rivalry.”

	As usual, Drunk Uncle got progressively more emotional as the segment went on, tossing out one-liners about Elizabeth Holmes (“I believe her”) and “Helen of Troy was white,” in a nod to the ongoing angry debate in some circles about the casting of historical characters in period movies and TV shows.

	But just as Drunk Uncle began to wallow, he was surprised by the appearance of two Brewers players , slugger Christian Yelich and second baseman Brice Turang, and the team’s manager, Pat Murphy.
	

	“Don’t worry Drunk Uncle,” Yelich told Moynihan. “It wasn’t a dream.”

	Murphy introduced himself to Drunk Uncle, saying that being a baseball manager is “kind of like being the Drunk Uncle of the team.”

	Moynihan looked up at the 6-foot-4 Yelich and declared, “I know you — you’re Pete Davidson.”

schema.headline: ‘SNL’ Celebrates Milwaukee Brewers’ World Series Win With Bobby Moynihan’s Drunk Uncle on Weekend Update

title: ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Finally Weighs in on Israel
description: The Halloween edition of “SNL” Weekend Update saw a cameo by Ben Marshall’s Pennywise as well as some jabs at President Trump’s recent obsession wi
body:
The Halloween edition of “SNL” Weekend Update saw a cameo by Ben Marshall’s Pennywise as well as some jabs at President Trump’s recent obsession with candidates’ posteriors.

	“Even Vice President JD Vance came out and said that he was jealous that President Trump has never complimented his butt. What the hell is going on! Your party is about to lose the midterms, stop playing ‘smash or pass’ with each other!” exclaimed co-anchor Colin Jost.
	

	Later on during Weekend Update, Michael Che made a joke about Israel that made Jost jokingly grimace.


	“This week, a record number of people voted in Israel’s election — which is great to see, regardless of if you’re on the right side, or the left side, or the genocide,” quipped Che.

	One of the reasons why the U.K.’s “Saturday Night Live” Weekend Update has lapped the U.S. version is that Jost and Che have largely avoided controversial topics like Israel, whereas the U.K.’s Weekend Update co-anchors have artfully mocked the likes of Ed Sheeran and Macklemore over their outsized roles in the conversation surrounding Israel’s war on Gaza.

	And this, it seems, is the best Jost and Che could finally come up with.

schema.headline: ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Finally Weighs in on Israel

title: Inde Navarrette Wins Halloween With Penis-Destroying Robot ‘SNL’ Sketch ‘The Inventor’s Wife’
description: After a pretty weak cold open that was crashed by Tom Hanks’ David S. Pumpkins, Donald Trump (who admitted he “might be gay”) and his MAGA minion N
body:
After a pretty weak cold open that was crashed by Tom Hanks’ David S. Pumpkins, Donald Trump (who admitted he “might be gay”) and his MAGA minion Nicki Minaj, and an amusing opening monologue where host Inde Navarrette took a swipe at Shane Gillis, the Halloween edition of “Saturday Night Live” aired a surprisingly fun sketch called “The Inventor.”

	The sketch opens with Navarrette delivering a eulogy for her dead husband, an “eccentric” inventor who “spent his final days in his workshop building god knows what,” adding, “My husband loved his inventions and he… liked his wife.”
	

	When she returns home from the wake, she sees that her husband’s left behind a gift for his widow in his workshop —a cute, Wall-E-like robot called the PD 44. The two become the best of friends, though she can’t figure out what PD’s “purpose” is.



	We jump six years into the future, and Navarrette’s lonely widow is finally ready to date. She matches with a nice-looking man named Tom Oakland (played by Ben Marshall) on a dating app, and the two go out on a romantic date. They seem to click, and she takes him back to her apartment for a nightcap to meet PD — when, all of a sudden, PD transforms into a giant, menacing killer robot, rips Tom’s penis off and hurls it into the moon.

	“PD stands for Penis Destroyer?!” exclaims Navarrette’s widow, before the robot shoots Tom with a laser beam until he explodes, covering her in blood.

	“He did love me… My husband loved me after all!” says the delighted woman.
	

	The sketch was a fine showcase for Navarrette’s crack timing and commitment to the bit, and one of the better “SNL” digital shorts in quite some time.

schema.headline: Inde Navarrette Wins Halloween With Penis-Destroying Robot ‘SNL’ Sketch ‘The Inventor’s Wife’

title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stars Relive Hollywood Ovation and Fan Chants for Yamazaki Takashi at Tokyo Festival
description: The cast of “Godzilla Minus Zero” brought the glow of a Hollywood standing ovation to the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival on Sunday, two day
body:
The cast of “Godzilla Minus Zero” brought the glow of a Hollywood standing ovation to the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival on Sunday, two days before Yamazaki Takashi’s follow-up to his Oscar-winning “Godzilla Minus One” opens in Japan.

	Kamiki Ryunosuke, who returns as lead character Shikishima Koichi, and Hamabe Minami, who reprises the role of his wife Noriko, had flown back to Japan only two days earlier from the film’s premiere at Los Angeles’ TCL Chinese Theatre.
	

	“The energy was simply extraordinary,” Kamiki said. “Feeling that raw enthusiasm firsthand made me realize all over again just how deeply Godzilla is loved around the world. It was an invaluable experience.”

	Applause in the 900-seat theater reportedly ran on without a break. Hamabe said the cast later met premiere-goers at an after-party, where many approached them with big smiles to share their reactions. Some had dressed in Godzilla-themed outfits or wore Godzilla badges.

	The red carpet was open to passersby, Kamiki recalled. Some fans held up large posters and asked for autographs, while chants of the director’s first name broke out from the crowd. “It wasn’t just a polite ‘Takashi,’” he said. “It was like: ‘TAKASHI! HEY, TAKASHI!’ It was roaring.” When Yamazaki went over to sign autographs, the crowd erupted again, leaving Kamiki convinced that “Takashi of the world is truly amazing.”

	The Tokyo event also marked the first stage appearance of child actor Nagatani Sae, who returns as Shikishima Akiko. Kamiki walked her onstage.
	

	In “Minus One,” which aired on Japanese TV’s “Friday Roadshow” on Friday, Akiko’s part consisted mostly of crying or single words such as “Where?” This time, the script gave her full dialogue. “We were like, ‘Really? Can she do this?’” Kamiki said. “But when we got on set, she had all her lines memorized perfectly and delivered them flawlessly.”

	Hamabe said Nagatani had barely left toddlerhood during the first shoot and was easily frightened by the many adults on set. “So reuniting on this film, I was amazed by how much of a wonderful young girl she had grown into,” she said. “She chatted with us so much, taught me various things, and was very dependable in her acting.”

	Nagatani said she wasn’t nervous during filming. She recalled Kamiki continuing to rub her back even after the cut was called on a scene in which Akiko cries. She then asked her co-stars how she could become a fine actor while still in elementary school. Kamiki told her she already outshone them both, and said that appearing in both “Minus One” and “Minus Zero” at her age was “an amazing achievement in itself.”

	According to Kamiki, the new film picks up two years after the events of “Minus One.” “I hope viewers can imagine what those two years were like for them, and see how the family stands together against what comes next,” he said. Hamabe put the gap at two to three years. She said the family had settled into everyday life together before Godzilla resurfaces to threaten it.

	Asked why the franchise has endured, Kamiki echoed the view of the director and fellow cast members that each Godzilla film mirrors the era in which it is made. “But personally, when I reflect on it, take Godzilla’s existence or the theme music: I cannot even remember when I first heard it or realized, ‘Oh, this is Godzilla’s theme song,’” he said. “It has always been alongside us, which is why I personally think it has remained loved for so long.”

	Hamabe said that from a human standpoint, Godzilla is overwhelming and impossible to defeat. “Yet, when Godzilla appears, humans unite and stand together to face it,” she said. “I think seeing that human resolve is the first thing that moves people’s hearts.”

	“Minus One,” the 30th Japanese live-action entry in the Godzilla franchise, grossed more than JPY7.65 billion ($50 million) at the local box office. It became the first Asian production to take home the visual effects prize at the 96th Oscars, and went on to collect more than 50 honors at home and abroad.
	

	“Minus Zero” is the first Japanese film to be certified as Filmed for Imax.

schema.headline: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stars Relive Hollywood Ovation and Fan Chants for Yamazaki Takashi at Tokyo Festival

title: Michael Mann Hospitalized After Accidentally Shooting Himself in the Leg at Los Angeles Gun Range
description: Michael Mann was hospitalized on Saturday after he accidentally shot himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the L.A. Police De
body:
Michael Mann was hospitalized on Saturday after he accidentally shot himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the L.A. Police Department.

	The director was trying to holster a firearm during a target practice at a sanctioned gun range when the weapon accidentally went off, as first reported by TMZ. The incident occurred around 4 p.m. at the Range L.A., and LAPD confirmed he was in stable condition at the time of the call. Mann has been an experienced shooter who has practiced on ranges for decades, and his wound was described as “subcutaneous and minor,” according to his reps.
	

	“On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann. He was treated and is being released,” Mann’s reps said in a statement.

	Mann is best known for directing such movies as “Heat,” “Thief,” “Manhunter,” “Miami Vice” and “The Insider.” He last directed 2023’s “Ferrari,” a sports biopic starring Adam Driver as Enzo Ferrari and Penelope Cruz as his wife Laura.

	The 83-year-old filmmaker is currently working on “Heat 2,” the long-awaited sequel to his 1995 crime drama starring Al Pacino and Robert De Niro. The first film, a box office hit, follows an explosive face-off between Los Angeles Police Department detective Lieutenant Vincent Hanna (Pacino) and professional thief Neil McCauley (De Niro). Mann adapted the screenplay for “Heat 2” from the 2022 novel of the same name that he co-wrote with Meg Gardiner. Described as a sequel and prequel to the original, the follow-up looks at the early lives of Pacino and De Niro’s characters. The cast is expected to include Leonardo DiCaprio, Christian Bale and Adam Driver.
	

	“The characters of ‘Heat’ are so alive to me,” Mann said during a 2025 masterclass at Lumiere Festival in France. “An idea occurred to me, based on the rapport between two lethal adversaries, Pacino’s Hannah and De Niro’s McCauley, about how to do both before the events of ‘Heat’ and after.”

schema.headline: Michael Mann Hospitalized After Accidentally Shooting Himself in the Leg at Los Angeles Gun Range

title: Valladolid Festival Prizes: Alain Gomis’ ‘Dao’ Wins Golden Spike, ‘La Gradiva’ Takes Silver
description: French-Senegalese filmmaker Alain Gomis’ “Dao,” an expansive family saga spanning Europe and Africa, was awarded the Golden Spike for best film at
body:
French-Senegalese filmmaker Alain Gomis’ “Dao,” an expansive family saga spanning Europe and Africa, was awarded the Golden Spike for best film at Spain’s 71st Valladolid International Film Festival (Seminci) while Marine Atlan’s acclaimed debut “La Gradiva” received the Silver Spike.

	Unfolding between a wedding in France and an ancestral memorial ceremony in Guinea-Bissau, Gomis’ three-hour film blurs fiction and documentary, gathering a sprawling cast of professional and non-professional performers to explore family ties, migration and the pull of inherited traditions. The international jury praised the film’s distinctive cinematic form, citing its use of rhythm, duration and movement to create an intimate yet immersive atmosphere.
	

	“Dao,” which world premiered in competition at Berlin, marks Gomis’ return to fiction features after “Félicité,” winner of the 2017 Berlinale Grand Jury Prize. Reviewing the new film, Variety’s Guy Lodge called it the director’s “most vibrantly expansive and accessible” work. The Party Film Sales handles international sales while Janus Films holds North American distribution rights.

	Atlan’s “La Gradiva” premiered at Cannes’ Critics’ Week, where it won its top Grand Prix, before receiving the Melbourne International Film Festival’s Bright Horizons Award in August. At Valladolid, the French-Italian feature also picked up the José Salcedo editing prize for Guillaume Lillo and the Rainbow Spike, recognizing LGBTQ-related cinema.



	

									‘La Gradiva’ Courtesy of Valladolid International Film Festival
	



	Set during a French school trip to Naples and Pompeii, the film follows a group of teenagers navigating desire, insecurity and the last moments of adolescence. “Seismically sensitive and deeply moving,” wrote Variety critic Jessica Kiang, who called it “one of the most piercingly accurate and immersive portrayals ever” of that precarious age. MK2 Films represents international sales.
	

	Argentine filmmaker Lisandro Alonso, whose credits include “Jauja” and “Eureka,” earned the Ribera del Duero best director award for “Double Freedom,” the well-received sequel to his 2001 debut “Freedom,” sold by Luxbox. 

	Acting honors went to Alba Rohrwacher for Stéphane Brizé’s “A Good Little Soldier,” in which she plays a corporate executive caught in a system of profit at any cost, and Swann Arlaud for Emmanuel Marre’s “A Man of His Time,” about a French engineer drawn into the Vichy regime.

	Marre’s film also picked up the cinematography award for Olivier Boonjing. Austrian filmmaker Sandra Wollner won the Miguel Delibes screenplay prize for “Everytime,” a drama exploring grief and memory through digital technology. The official competition jury gave a special mention to Tiago Guedes’ “Aquí.”

	Beyond the main competition, Thai filmmaker Sompot Chidgasornpongse took the Meeting Point prize for “9 Temples to Heaven,” which premiered in Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight. The contemplative family pilgrimage drama marks the fiction-feature debut of a longtime collaborator of Apichatpong Weerasethakul. Marc Ferrer’s “Cinemanía” received the Fundos Award, while Manon Coubia won the ESCAC directing prize for “Forest High.”

	Spanish debut “Salen las lobas” emerged as a double audience favorite, taking both the Meeting Point Audience Award and the Seminci Youth Prize. Directed by Claudia Estrada Tarascó, the film follows girls in a juvenile justice facility who bond over music and dreams of a Barcelona trap competition. Produced by Alba Sotorra’s Oceanika, it is sold internationally by MoreThan Films and is set for a Dec. 11 Spanish theatrical release through Silencio Cinema.

	In the Alchemies section, Ivan Marković’s “Promised Spaces,” a portrait of Cambodia’s rapidly transformed urban landscape, collected the Grand Prize. David Baute’s “Benigno,” about an elderly man preserving a disappearing way of life in the Canary Islands, received a special mention and the environmental Green Spike.

	Hassen Ferhani’s Algeria-France production “Alea Jacarandas” took the Time of History Grand Prize, with the special award going to Mariano Llinás’ “Life of Jorge Luis Borges.” Isabelle Stever’s “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming” received the FIPRESCI critics’ prize, while Markus Schleinzer’s “Rose” won the main competition Audience Award.
	

	Seminci unveiled its winners Saturday morning in Valladolid after organizers canceled the traditional closing gala following a deadly train accident in Toledo province. Held Oct. 23-31, the festival’s 71st edition was led by interim co-directors Mariona Viader and Javier H. Estrada following the death of José Luis Cienfuegos last December. 

	Organizers reported a provisional audience tally of 100,000, more than 120 film discussions and participation by over 90% of the directors represented in its official sections. The festival closed with the Spanish premiere of Gael García Bernal’s “Hombre al agua.”

	And the Awards:

title: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ and ‘Clayface’ Battle for No. 1 With $10.5 Million in Sleepy Halloween Weekend
description: A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” and DC’s comic book adaptation “Clayface” are vying for first place at the domestic box
body:
A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” and DC’s comic book adaptation “Clayface” are vying for first place at the domestic box office, with each film on track to collect around $10.5 million over the weekend. 

	Although it’ll be a close call, “You Can See Everything” has the slight edge with $10.6 million while expanding to 3,242 venues in its third frame while “Clayface” looks just behind with $10.4 million from 3,478 theaters in its sophomore outing, according to respective studio estimates. (The final results will be tallied on Monday.) “You Can See Everything” is already a box office winner, but it would be quite a feat for the non-fiction film to ascend to No. 1 in its third weekend in theaters.
	

	“That’s a rare achievement for any film, let alone a documentary running more than three hours,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian.

	Overall, it was another painfully slow Halloween for cinema owners without any new releases, as well as the misfortune of the holiday landing on Saturday. When Halloween coincides with the weekend, families prefer to go trick-or-treating rather than visit their local multiplex. Revenues between Friday and Sunday amounted to roughly $60 million, marking one of the slowest weekends of the year, according to Rentrak. However, it’s an improvement from 2025’s Halloween weekend, which resulted in $49 million across all films, led by Colleen Hoover adaptation “Regretting You” and “Black Phone 2.”

	“With costume parties, trick-or-treating and countless other Halloween activities, theaters were facing some pretty stiff competition for people’s time and attention,” Dergarabedian says.
	

	“You Can See Everything” has been the fall season’s breakout hit with $63.88 million domestically to date. It has yet to be released at the international box office. With euphoric word-of-mouth and repeat viewings from audiences who are trying to process the stranger-than-fiction film, “You Can See Everything” is expected to leave theaters as one of the biggest documentaries in decades. And it will be very profitable for A24, which produced the nearly three-hour movie for $7 million.

	“Clayface,” an R-rated origin story about the Batman villain, has generated $44.1 million in North America and $83 million globally. It’s shaping up to be a modest win for DC, having cost just $44 million to produce. That’s a much leaner price tag than DC’s other recent tentpoles, such as last year’s $225 million-budgeted “Superman” and July’s $175 million-budgeted “Supergirl.” The studio spent less on “Clayface” because the story is much darker than those family-friendly adventures, and because the character isn’t as well known compared to some of the company’s A-list superheroes. DC’s next big-screen endeavors will feature marquee names with next summer’s “Superman: Man of Tomorrow” and 2028’s “The Batman: Part II,” led by Robert Pattinson.

	Laika’s stop-motion animated fantasy “Wildwood” remained at No. 3 with $7.5 million in its sophomore outing, a 39% drop. So far, the well-reviewed film has earned $25 million domestically and $35 million globally. Since “Wildwood” has a huge $100 million production budget (stop-motion animation is labor-intensive and can take several years to produce), the movie likely won’t turn a profit in its theatrical run.

	Fourth place went to Black Bear’s offbeat romantic comedy “Wicker” with $4.1 million from 2,374 venues in its second weekend, a decline of just 28% from its debut. The film has earned $13.2 million domestically to date, a solid tally considering the low-budget project was acquired by Black Bear after Sundance for $2.5 million.

	Paramount’s video game reboot “Street Fighter” rounded out the top five with $3.2 million in its third frame, another harsh 63% drop. The movie has grossed $53 million in North America and $91.9 million worldwide. Although “Street Fighter” is nearing the $100 million mark, it’s not close to breaking even or getting into the black. Legendary and video game developer Capcom co-financed “Street Fighter” for $82 million, and theater owners keep around half of ticket sales.
	

	Elsewhere, Sony didn’t report grosses for the Jenna Ortega-led literary adaptation “Klara and the Sun” in what would have been the film’s second weekend of release. The film collapsed in its opening with $720,000 from 880 locations. The studio scaled back the theatrical footprint after critics derided the movie as “calamitous” and “confoundingly awful.” Director Taika Waititi claimed he doesn’t read reviews but, in a recent social media post, he referred to critics of his work as “sad lost souls who couldn’t achieve their dreams of becoming artists.” The movie cost $20 million to make and will wind up in the red for Sony. It’s the studio’s second consecutive misfire after Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Reckoning,” which left theaters with a paltry $9 million in North America and $17 million globally against a $30 million budget. Luckily, the studio’s losses on those films will be cushioned by two major winners, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” (the third-biggest movie ever with $2.5 billion) and Zach Cregger’s “Resident Evil” reboot ($400 million).

	In limited release, Sony Pictures Classics’s crime thriller “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” cracked the top 10 with $2 million from 1,112 theaters. John Turturro stars in the awards hopeful, which revolves around a pickpocket master who struggles to keep up with the changing times — phones are trackable, wallets rarely have cash and guns are hiding in plain sight. 

	Meanwhile, Netflix’s Oscar contender “La Bola Negra” added $418,000 from 38 theaters. So far, the generation-spanning queer drama has earned $1.2 million as the streamer rolls out the film at a glacial pace. Also this weekend, Netflix released Peter Berg’s war drama “The Mosquito Bowl,” which brought back $455,000 from 349 locations — a much wider footprint than “La Bola Negra.”

title: The Best Pop-Culture Advent Calendars for 2026: ‘Bluey,’ ‘The Nightmare Before Christmas,’ Marvel and More
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Why wait
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Why wait until Christmas to start unwrapping? Advent calendars make the case for treating yourself all December long, and this year’s lineup goes well beyond the usual bite-sized chocolates.

	This year, brands are finding increasingly creative ways to cash in on the tradition. Nespresso has teamed up with Swarovski for a sparkly caffeine fix, Lego is bringing holiday cheer to a galaxy far, far away, and Bloomingdale’s is packing more than $1,200 worth of luxury beauty products into a single box. Many of this year’s most coveted calendars are also reusable, with collectible figurines, ornaments and keepsakes designed to outlast the holiday season.
	

	Whether you’re shopping for a Disney obsessive, a beauty enthusiast or someone who simply likes opening presents, these advent calendars make the lead-up to Christmas almost as exciting as the big day itself. Below, find our favorite picks for 2026, from affordable stocking-stuffer alternatives to luxury splurges.


						
			
	

	
					

	For horror fans who would rather spend December with monsters than elves, this 24-day advent calendar offers a darker holiday countdown. Each compartment reveals a mystery miniature collectible, from masked figures to skeletons and supernatural creatures. 


						
			
	

	
					

	Tim Burton’s holiday classic gets a sugary twist with this 12-day countdown from Williams Sonoma. Inspired by “The Nightmare Before Christmas,” the calendar is packed with delightfully creepy confections, including Jack and Sally-shaped marshmallows, gummy spiders, sour worms, black licorice and pumpkin-shaped sweets. 


						
			
	

	
					

	Ariel, Cinderella, Moana and Mulan are getting together for the holidays in LEGO’s latest Disney Princess advent calendar. The 290-piece set features 24 daily surprises, including buildable accessories and miniature versions of beloved sidekicks like Sebastian, Mushu and Pua. Once all the doors are open, the packaging transforms into a board game that up to eight people can play.
	


						
			
	

	
					

	Even a galaxy far, far away celebrates Christmas. This year’s LEGO “Star Wars” advent calendar takes its inspiration from “The Mandalorian,” featuring Mando and Grogu in matching holiday sweaters (each emblazoned with the other’s likeness), along with Moff Gideon, Jawa figures and miniature spacecraft. The 293-piece set also includes a festive X-wing and several brick-built creatures, bringing a little seasonal cheer to the Outer Rim.

		

	

	
					
		

										LIMITED-EDITION						

					Disney Christmas Cookies 24-Day Advent Calendar		

		
	

	This limited-edition set features 24 mystery collectible pins designed to look like Christmas cookies, each presented on its own miniature baking pan. The $275 calendar comes packaged like a festive oven, complete with a display tray to show off the full collection once Christmas arrives.


						
			
	

	
					

	The Heeler family is celebrating Christmas with 24 days of surprises in this “Bluey” advent calendar. Among the goodies are eight exclusive flocked figures featuring Bluey, Bingo, Bandit, Chilli, Muffin and other fan-favorite characters, all dressed for the festive season. 


	

	
					

	The Avengers are taking a break from saving the world to celebrate the holidays. LEGO’s 2026 Marvel advent calendar assembles Spider-Man, Iron Man, Wolverine, Captain America, Ghost-Spider and Doctor Doom for 24 days of superhero-themed builds. Highlights include Spider-Man on skis, a snowball cannon, an X-Jet sleigh and a Christmas tree made with Wolverine’s signature claws. The 317-piece set is recommended for ages 6 and up.


			
			
			
			
	

	
					

	Halloween Town is coming to the Christmas tree. Hallmark’s “The Nightmare Before Christmas” countdown calendar includes 12 miniature, shatterproof ornaments inspired by Tim Burton’s beloved film, with a new character-themed decoration to unveil each day. Unlike the usual disposable advent treats, these collectibles can return to the tree year after year.


						
			
	

	
					

	Olaf has always been enthusiastic about all things warm and festive, so it makes sense that Disney’s resident snowman would get his own Christmas countdown. This 18-inch plush version of the “Frozen” character wears a Santa hat and features 12 numbered pockets, along with a soft Sven marker that moves from day to day. It’s a reusable decoration that doubles as a cuddly companion for younger “Frozen” fans.


						
			
	

	
					

	Funko’s miniature Bitty Pop! figures are getting the royal treatment with this Disney Princess holiday collection. Across 24 doors, collectors will uncover 10 tiny figures, nine stackable display pieces, three festive accessories and cases designed for a keychain and pin. 
	


	Not a pop-culture junkie? Find more advent calendars — spanning wellness, beauty and stationary — below:


						
			
	

	
					

	Bloomingdale’s is going big on beauty this holiday season. Its exclusive advent calendar packs 27 products from some of the industry’s most coveted names, including La Mer, Augustinus Bader, Sisley Paris and Armani Beauty. Retailing for $350, the assortment boasts a combined value of $1,252. 


						
			
	

	
					

	Charlotte Tilbury is bringing some Hollywood glamour to the holiday countdown with a 15-piece collection of the makeup artist’s cult-favorite products. Expect recognizable hits like the Pillow Talk lipstick, Beauty Light Wand, Airbrush Flawless Setting Spray and Charlotte’s Magic Cream, alongside skincare and makeup accessories. The red-and-gold, star-adorned case doubles as a jewelry box once the festivities are over.


						
			
	

	
					

	A good candle can make even the smallest apartment feel like a winter retreat. Voluspa’s 12-day calendar features a dozen petite candles in decorative glass vessels, spanning the fragrance brand’s bestselling Japonica and holiday collections. Scents include Mediterranean Lemon and Gingerbread Chalet, while a gold-plated wick trimmer rounds out the $185 set. Each candle offers approximately 25 hours of burn time.


						
			
	

	
					

	For those who prefer their holiday surprises shaken or stirred, Straightaway Cocktails offers a more grown-up take on the advent calendar. Its “12 Nights of Cocktails” countdown trades candy and collectibles for ready-to-drink cocktails, making it a festive option for cocktail enthusiasts or holiday hosts. No bartending skills required — just a glass and an occasion to celebrate.


						
			
	

	
					

	Stationery obsessives, this one’s for you. Papier’s $195 advent calendar is packed with more than $375 worth of writing accessories, notebooks and desk essentials, from rollerball pens and journals to sticky tabs, bookmarks and wax-seal stickers. There’s even a miniature jigsaw puzzle and playing cards in the mix, with each gift tucked inside a reusable drawer.


						
			
	

	
					

	YSL Beauty’s $400 advent calendar is among the more extravagant options this season, offering $645 worth of makeup, fragrances and skincare inside a glossy burgundy case. The lineup includes full-size lip products and a Couture Mini Clutch eyeshadow palette, plus miniature versions of the brand’s Libre, Black Opium, Y and MYSLF fragrances. 


						
			
	

	
					

	Nespresso has enlisted Swarovski to give its annual coffee countdown a little sparkle. The 2026 Vertuo calendar features an assortment of coffee capsules to discover throughout December, with an exclusive collaborative accessory waiting behind the final door. And don’t let the luxe partnership scare you away — it’s only $55.
	


						
			
	

	
					

	Alo is extending its wellness-focused lifestyle beyond leggings and workout gear with a seven-day advent calendar. The shortened countdown puts self-care at the center of the holiday season, offering an alternative to the usual sweets and collectibles.

title: Martha Stewart Posts and Deletes 'Hungry' Poor Person Halloween Costume Photo

body:
Martha Stewart
                          Deletes 'Hungry' Poor Person Halloween Costume Pic
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 1, 2026
                            5:12 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Martha Stewart has received some backlash after posting and then quickly deleting a photo of her Halloween costume -- a "hungry" poor person.
      
    
            In the since scrubbed snap ... Martha appears in tattered clothes, with dirt on her face, and holding up a sign on a clipboard that reads ... "I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!"
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The pic had apparently been included in an Instagram carousel promoting candles she sells on QVC before it was deleted ... but not before several IG users screengrabbed the post.
      

            In the caption, Martha, who has an estimated net worth of $400 million, wrote ... "My QVC candles are perfect for Halloween!!!" Her accompanying poor person get-up? Not so perfect.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            The post recirculated on Reddit, where scores of users were quick to slam the costume as "out of touch," "offensive" and "gross."
      
    
            We've reached out to Martha's rep for comment ... so far, no word back.

body:
Doors Guitarist Robby Krieger
                          Wife Dead at 79
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 31, 2026
                            5:24 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Lynn Krieger -- the wife of the legendary guitarist of The Doors, Robby Krieger -- is dead ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ ... Lynn died in her sleep Thursday after battling a longtime illness.
      
    
            We're told paramedics were called to Robby and Lynn's Beverly Hills home just before noon for a possible cardiac arrest, but Lynn was already dead when fire and police personnel arrived.
      
    
            Law enforcement also received a call for a natural death. Her official cause of death is not known at this time.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Lynn met Robby and the rest of The Doors at a New York City nightclub in 1967. They married in 1972 and had one child together -- a son named Waylon.
      
    
            She was 79.
      
    
            RIP

title: Influencer Khiana Smith in ICU with Life-Threatening Brain Infection During Bali Vacation
description:
Influencer Khiana Smith
                          Contracts Deadly Brain Infection
body:
Influencer Khiana Smith
                          Contracts Deadly Brain Infection
                          ... While on Vacay in Bali
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 1, 2026
                            9:03 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Rising fitness influencer Khiana Smith remains hospitalized in the ICU after suffering a brain infection ... and admits she feels "absolutely helpless."
      
    
            Taking to TikTok ... Khiana said that she has been "bedbound in ICU in Bali with a brain infection that could have killed me."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The influencer -- who boasts nearly 87,000 followers across TikTok and Instagram -- said that she contracted bacterial meningitis and has since been diagnosed with pneumonia during her Bali trip.
      

            What started as a headache turned into "extreme head pains, dizziness, slurred speech, slurred vision, and a severe sensitivity to light."
      
    
            After spending 9 days in the ICU, Khiana said she "lost a lot of memory, like, I really struggle to remember things."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As she remains hospital-bound, Khiana added ... "I feel absolutely helpless, and I just wanna go home."
      
    
            Rest up, Khiana!

body:
Michael Mann
                          Accidentally Shoots Himself in Leg at L.A. Gun Range
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 1, 2026
                            5:09 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 1, 2026
                                8:01 AM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
          UPDATE
  
    
            7:22 AM PT -- Michael Mann's rep tells TMZ ... "On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann. He was treated and is being released."
      
    
            Michael Mann was sent to the hospital after he accidentally shot himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources tells TMZ ... the "Heat" director -- who is an an experienced target shooter for decades -- had been apparently trying to holster his weapon during target practice at a sanctioned gun range around 4 PM when the firearm went off.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He was later transported by an ambulance to a local hospital ... but thankfully his injury is subcutaneous and minor.
      

            The LAPD confirms the incident to us ... cops and the LAFD responded to The Range LA after reports of the shooting.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            They say the victim -- who had no intention of harming himself -- was injured during a training accident when he accidentally discharged a firearm into his own leg.
      
    
            We've reached out to Michael's rep for comment ... so far, no word back.
